intent: Bring mutate_session_autopsy_hooks.py under the 250-line cap by extracting its mutation operators, leaving the mutation results unchanged.
scope: Non-goal: changing any mutation, or the hooks and tests they exercise
changes: Moved the eight mutation operators (_gut, _drop_transcript_guard, _widen_count, _drop_numeric_guard, _drop_readable_guard, _always_announce, _unguarded_and_always_announce), the Mutation NamedTuple, the MUTATIONS table and the _GUTTED constant into _session_autopsy_mutations.py.
Promoted _END_HOOK/_START_HOOK to END_HOOK/START_HOOK and _MUTATIONS to MUTATIONS, since they now cross a module boundary, and declared __all__ for the four exported names.

The driver keeps _TEST_FILE, _OUTCOME, and everything that touches the filesystem or runs pytest. The new module is pure text transforms, which makes the 'deployed hooks are never modified' guarantee easier to see.

Gave the new module a #!/usr/bin/env python3 shebang, matching the sibling _schema_validation.py. That is what satisfies ruff's INP001 here -- ruff exempts files it recognises as scripts -- so no __init__.py and no per-file-ignore were needed.

verification.command: python3 meta/scripts/mutate_session_autopsy_hooks.py, diffed against the same run from a detached worktree at HEAD
verification.evidence: Byte-identical output. All eight mutations run in the same order and kill the same named tests (gut-end 2, gut-start 1, end-no-transcript-guard 4, start-count-ge-zero 1, start-no-numeric-guard 1, start-no-readable-guard 0, start-always-announce 3, start-unguarded-announce 5), ending in 'PASS: all 12 tests killed by at least one mutation'.

ruff, mypy, pylint and bandit all pass. Three real defects were caught and fixed rather than suppressed: the new module needed its own `import re`; the driver still annotates _apply with Mutation and so needed that name imported too (F821 from ruff, name-defined from mypy, E0602 from pylint -- three tools, one bug); and INP001 was answered with the sibling's shebang convention.
driver 178, mutations 100. Neither appears in the violation list.

verification.command: grep for importers and patch targets
verification.evidence: Nothing in the repository imports this module and no test patches it; it is only a pre-commit entry point (.pre-commit-config.yaml:276). So no test file needed editing, and the decision-8 bound on test edits does not come into play.

risks: The bare `from _session_autopsy_mutations import ...` relies on Python putting the script's own directory on sys.path. That holds when the file is run as a script, which is the only way it is used -- verified by actually running it from the repository root, the same way .pre-commit-config.yaml invokes it. The sibling validate_evidence.py imports _schema_validation the same way.

The first run after the split failed with NameError on `re`, caught only by executing the script -- ast.parse had reported the file as fine. A missing import in a moved block is invisible to a parse check.
A PostToolUse formatter fired on the new module immediately after the `import re` edit; the import was re-checked with grep before proceeding, per the known trap.
rollback: git revert the commit; the driver returns to its 253-line form and the sibling disappears.
After rollback, run python3 meta/scripts/mutate_session_autopsy_hooks.py and confirm it still ends in 'PASS: all 12 tests killed by at least one mutation'.
